newsitem.title: UK: Med oil products fall with futures, except fuel.
newsitem.headline: Med oil products fall with futures, except fuel.

text.p: Mediterranean oil products were all weaker on Monday, apart from steady fuel oil, traders said.
Gasoline prices fell with futures. Little movement was seen although traders said they saw continuing demand for low octane barrels.
Naphtha was weaker too. A Skikda cargo was sold on Friday by a trader to another trader at $208.50 cif NWE. Offers of full range material were later heard at cif high +$2.50-$3 cif NWE.
Gas oil weakened in line with outright prices in northern Europe which tumbled on falling benchmark IPE futures, but traders said the market was relatively quiet.
"Players appear to be holding back to see where the Iraqi crisis will go next," one trader said.
One trader said he bought two Russian cargoes on Friday for roughly quotes cif high +$2.0, basis Genoa. A Russian cargo, which loaded in Tuapse on Friday, was reported to be on offer.
Traders said low sulphur supply was still tight, but added focus was on 0.2 percent material as Mediterranean countries stocked up on heating oil ahead of the winter.
Fuel oil resisted the downwards pull of crude futures with prices broadly steady.

Dealers said fundamentals were showing now that all the bullish tones of last week's Middle East tension were pulled away. Bunkering quality material was still scarce and able to command around quotes high fob Med +$3. Demand for non-bunker spec was seen essentially into Romanian although no deals were done. On Friday a poor quality high sulphur 50,000 tonne cargo was sold at high fob Med +75 cents and on Monday the talk was of quotes +50-70 cents.
Details of the winners of the Suez sell tender of eight plus three 30,000-tonne cargoes have filtered into the market. The cargoes were won at between mean fob Med +$3.5 and $4.25.
